title: Global coefficient integrability is impossible as a compact-torus continuation target

integrability_obstruction.baseline: K1389 defines B_R with a leading constant 1, so integral_0^infinity B_R dt diverges for every solution, including the vacuum
integrability_obstruction.nontrivial_mode: Choose a unit Q-eigenvector v with nonzero integer charge q and set A=0, phi(t,x)=a(t)v constant on T3 with real a
integrability_obstruction.reduced_equation: The Maxwell current vanishes identically and the matter equation reduces to a''+(m^2+mu q^2)a+lambda a^3=0
integrability_obstruction.global_periodic_solution: For m>0, mu>0 and lambda>0, every nonzero finite-energy oscillator solution is global, bounded and periodic
integrability_obstruction.baseline_removed_obstruction: Even after removing the artificial leading 1 from B_R, the term ||Qphi||_infinity=|q a(t)| has positive period average, so its time integral diverges
integrability_obstruction.logical_effect: Finite integral B_R is a sufficient finite-interval Gronwall condition, not a necessary global continuation condition and not an achievable global target on the compact torus
integrability_obstruction.reroute: Global propagation must allow nonintegrable bounded coefficients, for example by finite-interval iteration with a uniform low norm, a modified high energy, normal-form/resonance control or a different global invariant
integrability_obstruction.boundary: This obstruction does not prove global large-data propagation for the coupled system and does not exclude dispersive L1_t estimates after changing the spacetime from T3 to a noncompact geometry
